panels.title: Executed-test pass rate
panels.description:
This is NOT the bench generation gate. It measures whether the generated Robot test passed when it ran, over whatever range the dashboard time picker is set to — narrowing the range changes this number. Spine is execution_records; timestamp is TEXT holding UTC values in two shapes (verified 2026-08-10: 99 rows naive, 24 rows with an explicit +00:00 offset, no other suffix seen). The cast strips any trailing Z/offset and reinterprets the remainder as UTC explicitly, so the result does not depend on the query session's timezone setting.

Coverage: 109 of 123 execution records join to neither workflow_metrics nor test_runs, and 312 of 330 learning_metrics rows have no metrics row. Those 109 are real runs — 30 distinct queries across 9 domains with 62 passes, spanning 2026-02-23 to 2026-07-15 — not pollution, so they are counted here rather than joined away. What they blend is engine eras. The default now-1y window admits every one of them, so narrowing the time picker is a deliberate act, not a floor this dashboard applies for you.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE test_status = 'passed') / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS pass_pct FROM execution_records WHERE (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()

SELECT test_status, count(*) AS runs FROM execution_records WHERE (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY runs DESC

panels.title: Failure categories
panels.description: Categories are also present on some passed rows, so this filters to failures explicitly rather than assuming a category implies a failure.

targets.rawSql: SELECT coalesce(failure_category, '(none recorded)') AS category, count(*) AS failures, round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct FROM execution_records WHERE test_status <> 'passed' AND (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY failures DESC

SELECT failed_keyword, count(*) AS failures, count(DISTINCT domain) AS domains FROM execution_records WHERE test_status <> 'passed' AND failed_keyword IS NOT NULL AND (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY failures DESC

SELECT domain, count(*) AS runs, round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE test_status = 'passed') / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS pass_pct FROM execution_records WHERE (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY runs DESC

panels.title: Pass rate by generated code structure

targets.rawSql: SELECT coalesce(code_structure, '(unclassified)') AS structure, count(*) AS runs, round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE test_status = 'passed') / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS pass_pct FROM execution_records WHERE (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY runs DESC

panels.title: Recent failures, with the query that produced them

targets.rawSql: SELECT (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS at, workflow_id, user_query, failure_category, failed_keyword, error_message FROM execution_records WHERE test_status <> 'passed' AND (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() ORDER BY at DESC LIMIT 100

panels.title: Aggregate error logs
panels.description: Aggregate ERROR lines from both services. The filter is a literal substring match over raw log text, not a log-level filter: it does not catch CRITICAL, and on this stack every line containing CRITICAL was LLM prompt text echoed by verbose agent output rather than a log record. The caveat that matters more: when the observability compose stack is running, a bench sweep targets the containerised backend on 127.0.0.1:5000 — the same address run_bench.py uses by default — so bench log lines land in this feed alongside production ones. No label separates them. Use the per-run log panel on the trace dashboard when you need certainty about which run a line belongs to.
